concept.heading: Core Pattern
concept.body: Use two pointers (usually **left** and **right**) that move towards each other or in the same direction. Works on **sorted arrays** or when you need to compare elements from both ends.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.keyInsight: Compare chars from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric. If all match, it's a palindrome.

problems.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
problems.keyInsight: Since array is sorted, use two pointers from ends. Sum too small? Move left pointer right. Sum too big? Move right pointer left.

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.keyInsight: Sort array. Fix one number, then use Two Sum II (two pointers) on the rest. Skip duplicates at all levels to avoid duplicate triplets.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.keyInsight: Start with widest container (L=0, R=end). Always move the SHORTER side inward - moving the taller side can only make things worse (width shrinks & height can't increase).

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.keyInsight: Water at position i = min(maxLeft, maxRight) - height[i]. Use two pointers to track maxLeft and maxRight without extra arrays. Process the side with the smaller max first.

code.python:
def trap(height):
    l, r = 0, len(height) - 1
    left_max, right_max = height[l], height[r]
    water = 0

    while l < r:
        if left_max < right_max:
            l += 1
            left_max = max(left_max, height[l])
            water += left_max - height[l]
        else:
            r -= 1
            right_max = max(right_max, height[r])
            water += right_max - height[r]

    return water
